historical_reviews.deepseek: Selects a generic USB class but cannot prove which removable device or artifact booted; credential protection, state readback, safe removal and restoration are missing.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly requires stable USB identity and a non-destructive boot marker rather than accepting a selector return or any removable-media boot.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: USB enumeration order is unstable and may include internal devices. Acceptance must bind physical port and serial to firmware device path and artifact identity; otherwise a different USB or fallback device could satisfy the visible boot symptom.

original_test_intent: Validate that the BMC's enabled one-time USB setting boots the approved SUT from the intended removable device and approved artifact, without installation or persistent boot changes, then removes the device and restores normal boot.
original_method: Map the exact USB port, VID/PID/serial and firmware device path, validate an immutable compatible artifact and non-writing boot marker, capture boot baseline, obtain approval, apply/read back the protected one-time USB override, reboot once under POST/console observation, prove the mapped device and artifact, exit safely, power down or follow the approved removal boundary, remove USB, verify override consumption and restore the original OS path.
manual_activity: The owner approves the exact USB fixture and reboot; an operator confirms physical port/device, observes the boot marker, prevents disk writes and controls safe removal, recovery and verdict.
required_inputs: USB port, VID/PID, serial and firmware device path
Baseline boot order and removable-device population
safety_requirements: Do not infer a specific target from generic usb
Inventory all removable and internal USB boot candidates
Use immutable approved media and protected credentials
Read back one-time scope before reboot
Stop on wrong device/artifact, installer, disk-write prompt, boot failure or timeout
Do not hot-remove unless the fixture procedure permits it
Clear override, remove media and restore baseline
Preserve logs and do not automatically retry
agent_execution_scope: Collect boot and USB inventory baseline
Apply/read back one approved one-time USB setting after confirmation
Request and perform one approved reboot
Collect structured state while operator proves POST/console artifact marker
Verify safe exit, removal, override consumption and normal OS recovery
engineer_actions: Approve exact port/device/artifact and maintenance window
Observe intended USB boot and prevent writes

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: bootdev usb requests only a class and may not be supported uniformly; the literal command exposes credentials, resets immediately and lacks exact device/artifact proof, readback, removal and restoration.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the vendor-supported protected one-time USB control only after mapping it to the approved port/device; correlate readback, POST device identity and artifact marker, then exit/remove and restore.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Usb, Enabled/Save, reboot and 10/20-minute estimates remain; specific path becomes the approved USB device and artifact.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Record port topology, VID/PID/serial, firmware device path, artifact hash, override readback, POST selection, artifact landmark and final physical removal in one chain.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes generic USB boot attributable to one removable fixture without adding installation scope.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A visible USB-like boot screen or generic selector cannot exclude another removable/internal USB device or a firmware fallback.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Enumeration can change with hubs and internal USB devices; a device may contain multiple partitions or stale installers, so serial plus artifact identity and a defined marker are both required.

project_override_considerations: The Project must name the physical port/device and safe artifact. Installation remains a separate approval, and the copied PXE regression note does not define USB acceptance.
expected_evidence: Approved target/window, USB port/topology, VID/PID/serial, firmware path and artifact integrity
Protected one-time USB write/readback and reboot request
POST/console evidence binding the selected USB device to the approved non-writing artifact marker
Proof no installer or disk write occurred
Safe exit/removal, consumed override and original OS restoration
Health, audit/SEL/OS logs, recovery actions and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and procedure consistently request USB boot. The specific path is the project-selected USB fixture; the PXE note is copied context rather than a competing target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: USB identity, artifact, mapping and recovery are normal project inputs; the workflow remains identifiable without guessing them.

review_improvement: Transforms a generic USB selector into a device- and artifact-bound reversible boot check with explicit safe removal and no-write boundaries.
independent_technical_reasoning: Firmware often collapses many removable and internal USB devices into one boot class. Port topology and stable serial distinguish the fixture, while the artifact hash and console landmark distinguish its contents. Both are needed because either device enumeration or media content can independently be wrong despite a successful boot.
